newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas eyes jobs tender at three airports.
newsitem.headline: Qantas eyes jobs tender at three airports.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd said on Tuesday it was considering seeking tenders for ground work in three Australian airports and would set up a steering committee to oversee the process.

"Qantas will consult with unions over plans to introduce competitive tenders for some ground services at Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth airports," a Qantas spokesman told Reuters after a hearing in the Australian Industrial Relations Commission (IRC) in Sydney.
The spokesman declined to give details of Qantas' plans, but said the advertising process would begin on Friday.

The Australian Services Union (ASU) on Monday said Qantas would seek tenders for customer service and ramp services work in the three airports, and that about 1,000 of its members would be affected by the move.
ASU officials said a job tender would threaten its members' jobs and that workers would be forced to bid for their jobs against large multinationals.
"Our members say this process is only designed to drive wages and conditions down and force redundancies," ASU National Secretary Paul Slape said.
Earlier this month, Qantas said it would retrench 132 staff and 53 apprentices from its engineering and maintainance division in order to remain viable and improve productivity and efficiency.
British Airways Plc owns 25 percent of Qantas. Qantas shares closed one cent lower at A$2.75 on Tuesday.
